Neither player is expected to play against the Raiders on Thursday, and Thursday’s missed practice seems to clinch that. The 49ers’ receiving crops are in dire straits, with Christian Kirk also not practicing with his knee injury.

Headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss believes TreVeyon Henderson’s illness might be related to the “adversity” he has faced this season.
News Snippet: Reiss was asked about Henderson’s status during his weekly appearance on the local radio show, Toucher & Hardy. According to Reiss, Henderson has faced a lot of new challenges this season, including recurring ankle issues and limited playing time, and the adversity has been tough for Henderson to deal with. Some might remember that similar reports surfaced regarding Bucky Irving, beset by multiple injuries, last season. Henderson might need more time before he resumes playing. Stay tuned. He was officially listed as a non-participant on Thursday.

Headline: Drew Lock told reporters that his elbow “felt good” after Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: “It’s doing good. I’m excited to be back out there,” Lock said. “Felt great to get under center, rip some balls yesterday. Feels good.” Lock noted that he’ll go through a normal week of practice, and assuming there’s no setbacks, he’ll be under center in place of Sam Darnold (rib/quad) for Week 9 against the Cardinals. If Lock can’t go, it’ll be Jalen Milroe.

Headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: It’s back-to-back missed practices for the 24-year-old ahead of Week 9’s contest against the Buccaneers. It seems more than likely that Monangai comes back for Week 10 after the bye, but if he can get a full session in, there’s a chance he rolls against Tampa Bay come Sunday.

Headline: Breece Hall (quad) said he is ready to go for Week 9 against the Chiefs.
News Snippet: We expect to see Hall listed as a full participant on today’s injury report. An update will be provided if that is not the case. Earlier today, Jets OC Frank Reich discussed Hall and Braelon Allen’s expected usage, saying having the two players is “a great problem to have,” referring to the duo as “two No. 1 backs.” That said, Reich added that Hall “is obviously the bell cow,” but the backfield usage will be a “mix” of both players. Jets coach Aaron Glenn will reportedly share his ideal backfield split with Reich, who will work with the position coaches to make it happen. Hall likely belongs in the high-end RB2 tier while Allen remains FLEX-viable.

Headline: Bam Knight (concussion) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: It appears it’ll be another DNP for Knight as he entered the concussion protocol following Sunday’s win over the Cowboys in Week 8. The 25-year-old tailback seems unlikely to be able to go in Week 9 against the Seahawks, but there should be further updates on Knight’s status soon.

Headline: DJ Turner (heel) practiced in full on Thursday.
News Snippet: The Bengals No. 1 cornerback is firmly on track to play in Week 9 against the Falcons. While Drake London would get a matchup boost if Turner were to sit out, Turner’s presence does not drop London out of the WR1 tier.

Headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh indicated that Omarion Hampton will get more touches.
News Snippet: Harbaugh reportedly made comments to this effect earlier in the week. When asked for his thoughts on the matter, OC Mike McDaniel said he is “excited about someone dictating the rotation” and added that Hampton has “had a really great week of prep.” Hampton hasn’t scored double-digit half-PPR points since Week 4. Whether the potential usage increase can get him back to 10.0-plus points remains to be seen, but this week’s comments are at least somewhat encouraging.

Headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
News Snippet: Barkley is again on track to play through his injuries on game day. The Eagles’ offensive centerpiece totaled 54 scrimmage yards, one catch and one touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders. He may have trouble solidifying a spot in the RB1 tier, given the state of the Eagles’ offense, but he remains a high-end RB2 at worst, based on talent and usage.

Headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) was able to participate in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: A rare bit of good news on the injury front for the 49ers. McCaffrey was given the day off Wednesday, but even if this is just a limited session, it’s a good start for what could be a a Week 9 date against the Raiders that sees the tailback get a smorgasbord of touches due to the issues involving several injured receivers.

Headline: Bears placed RB Zavier Scott (thumb) on injured reserve
News Snippet: Scott has not played on offense at all this season, but he has successfully carved out a role on special teams. According to the Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs, the Bears have reason to believe that Scott’s injured reserve stint “will be on the shorter side.”

Headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) resumed practicing on Thursday.
News Snippet: Wright is on track to be available for the Dolphins’ Week 9 game against the Lions, although he is mostly functioning as an infrequently used backup rusher while also serving as the team’s top returner. He is a mid-tier bench stash at this time.

Headline: Malik Nabers (undisclosed) was seen working off to the side with trainers on Thursday.
News Snippet: The Giants have limited Nabers’ practice reps from time to time this season. Although he may end up being listed as a non-participant, we are not currently concerned about his Week 9 availability. The Giants’ No. 1 wide receiver is fully dressed in his typical practice attire. An update will be provided when more info is released.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Kyler Murray (hamstring) “will be ‘week-to-week’ now.”
News Snippet: Murray reportedly experienced soreness in his hamstring following the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions. Carson Wentz will start for the Vikings’ Week 9 Monday Night Football game against the Bills, and potentially longer. If Wentz plays well, Murray could be relegated to the backup role. Murray does not necessarily need to be stashed on benches in two-quarterback leagues at this time. This situation is not ideal for him.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Carson Wentz will start for the Vikings in Week 9 against the Bills.
News Snippet: On Monday, Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell told reporters that Kyler Murray is dealing with a “sore hamstring.” After breaking the news that Wentz will start for the Vikings’ Monday Night Football game, Schefter revealed that Murray is considered “week-to-week.” Unless Wentz flops and Murray’s strained hamstring recovers quickly, Wentz is seemingly in line to start for more than one game. If he plays well enough, he could end up starting for the rest of the season. Wentz’s installation upgrades the fantasy prospects for Vikings pass catchers. Wentz warrants QB2 treatment at this time.

Headline: Deshaun Watson (concussion) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: Cleveland’s Mary Kay Cabot indicated yesterday that Shedeur Sanders is seemingly slated to start in Week 9 against the Saints. If that ends up being the case, and Sanders can play well enough, it might be possible for him to steal the starting job from Watson this week. Sanders would be QB2-viable against the Saints.

Headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) did not practice Thursday.
News Snippet: Wilson did not practice on Wednesday and will go down as a DNP today as well. He is a long-shot to suit up for the Jets’ Week 9 game against the Chiefs. His absence will free up targets for Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. The two have alternated spike weeks and zeroes over their past two games. Now both should have stable fantasy floors for at least one game.

Headline: Jonathan Taylor said he has not requested a trade.
News Snippet: Taylor didn’t dwell on the question for more than a word, but he did confirm that no trade request has been made. The team’s desire to trade him is ultimately about rebuilding the roster after going all in on the ill-fated “Daniel Jones era.” With several teams reportedly interested and the Colts strongly motivated to recoup draft capital for the coming years, we expected a deal to get done before Tuesday’s deadline. For now, fantasy managers can keep Taylor in their lineups, as there’s been no indication that Taylor will be put on ice to protect his trade value.

Headline: 49ers GM John Lynch said it’s likely that Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will not play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
News Snippet: Lynch said the same about Mike Evans. Samuel hasn’t played or practiced since going down with a hamstring injury in Week 5. It’s unclear when he will return to the field. The fact that the 49ers didn’t place him on injured reserve when he suffered the injury suggests they expected him to miss fewer than four games. Week 9 will be his third absence.

Headline: 49ers GM John Lynch said it’s likely that Mike Evans (Achilles) will not play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
News Snippet: The same is true of Deebo Samuel, who has a calf injury. Evans has been dealing with the Achilles issue for a few weeks. The fact that a Week 8 bye wasn’t enough to get him back on the field suggests this will be something he deals with for potentially the rest of the year. Demarcus Robinson is expected to return from IR this week. Robinson, Christian Kirk, Jordan Watkins, and Brandin Cooks will all be in the mix for starting roles this week.

Headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: Robinson should be good to go for Week 9, though we won’t get official word on his status until tomorrow. He’ll reclaim the RB2 role in Atlanta once he gets cleared for action. Robinson will be a touchdown-or-bust RB4 if active.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Carson Wentz is “trending toward” starting in Week 9 against the Bills.
News Snippet: Kyler Murray suffered a hamstring injury in Week 8, but even Schefter alluded to the idea that this would be a soft benching for Murray. Schefter added that it “looks like there’s a question at the quarterback position” for Minnesota. Healthy or not, it sounds like Wentz is going to be under center versus Buffalo. Wentz made one start earlier in the season while Murray was sidelined with a concussion. He only threw for 133 yards on 19 attempts, but Wentz found the end zone three times. Murray hasn’t thrown three passing touchdowns in a game since the end of the 2024 season. Wentz’s gunslinging style will likely be a win for fantasy managers hoping to get more out of Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, especially in a potential shootout with the Bills.

Headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Colts plan to wait until after Week 9 against the Cowboys “before revisiting the offers on the table and making the trades that make sense on Monday and Tuesday.”
News Snippet: Long story short, the Colts are trying to wring every last ounce of draft capital out of their roster and think teams will up their offers after Sunday’s games. Schultz named Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs, and Grover Stewart as players who could be on the move. Daniel Jones’s name has also come up, though it’s hard to imagine another team paying even a late-round pick for his services given how dreadful he has been this year. All signs point to Taylor being moved early next week, but it’s clear the Colts are going to play hardball in trade talks. We still suspect he’s playing for a new team by Week 10.

Headline: Grady Jarrett (groin) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
News Snippet: Jarrett played in Week 8 against the Seahawks after missing Week 7 with a knee injury and now is an estimated DNP with a groin injury to open Week 9. He still has a chance to play, but will need at least a limited practice to appear against the Buccaneers.

Headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
News Snippet: Monangai was an estimated DNP on Wednesday, still not practicing in any capacity since Week 4. He has missed four consecutive games and is trending to miss a fifth one in Week 9 against the Buccaneers. In any injury taking this long for a return, a full practice is the best indicator of a return but the Bears may just wait until after their Week 10 bye to bring Monangai back. D’Andre Swift is in line for a workhorse game once again.

Headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Gainwell played through the hip injury last week to the tune of 25 carries. He starts out the week limited, but fantasy managers should expect to see the 27-year-old to play in Week 9 against the Bears.

Headline: Leonard Williams (stinger) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
News Snippet: Williams suffered a stinger in Week 8 and was an estimated DNP for the Seahawks’ walkthrough practice on Wednesday. The veteran will need to practice in some capacity to have a chance to play in Week 9 against the Cardinals. If not, the Seahawks’ interior defensive line will be reinforced by Mike Morris, who notched his first career sack against the Bears in Week 8.

Headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
News Snippet: Also not practicing is OT Charles Cross (ankle). Both missed Week 8 against the Bears and are still out with their respective injuries to open the week. They will need to practice in some fashion to have a chance at returning for the Seahawks offense in Week 9.

Headline: Drew Lock (elbow) was limited in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
News Snippet: Despite being listed as limited with a right elbow injury, Lock is expected to start in place of Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) in Week 9 against the Cardinals. Lock has been dealing with the elbow injury for a couple weeks and was the emergency third quarterback in Week 8 as a result. Fantasy managers can still expect Lock to start, but if the injury is not healed, Jalen Milroe is the next quarterback up for the Seahawks.

Headline: Reggie Virgil (back) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Virgil practiced fully after colliding with the goalpost in the Cardinals’ Week 8 win over the Cowboys. It’s a good sign that his back is not a major issue heading into the week. He’s in line to play in Week 9 against the Seahawks.

Headline: Bam Knight (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Knight entered concussion protocol after a hit to the head in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Starting out as a DNP this week means he still has a few steps to go to clear protocol by Sunday. Unless he can progress through protocol quickly, Knight is on the wrong side of questionable for Week 9 against the Seahawks.

Headline: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reports Josh Jacobs is “operating under the assumption” he won’t miss more games despite additional allegations of abuse against him.
News Snippet: Jacobs is facing additional allegations of verbal and physical abuse that could jeopardize his playing status moving forward. He told Demovsky that he is “operating under the assumption that he won’t have to sit out any more games than the six he already missed while on the NFL commissioner exempt list.” Jacobs has defended himself against the allegations after his attorneys also dismissed the claims. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said earlier this week he expects Jacobs to remain on the roster as the league reviews this round of allegations. Jacobs has missed six games on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and will continue to play while the NFL looks into the new claims.

Headline: Arthur Maulet retired after nine seasons in the NFL.
News Snippet: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports that Maulet is retiring. The 33-year-old slot cornerback began his career with the Saints and Colts and ended it with the Lions, but made the bulk of his impact from 2019-2024 with the Jets, Steelers, and Ravens. Maulet made major noise as a hard-hitting cornerback in the AFC North, going from the Steelers to the Ravens in 2023 and starting a playoff game for Mike Macdonald’s historic Ravens defense. He retires with five career interceptions and five sacks.

Headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Burks was limited-DNP-limited due to the foot injury last week, but played through it for five targets in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles. He starts out this week as a DNP as the Commanders manage his injury. Given he already played a game with the injury, Burks is still likely to play in Week 9, though he will need to get a practice in later this week to feel better about his chances of playing against the Rams.

Headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Njoku had his practice window opened this week, giving the Chargers 21 days to activate him off injured reserve. He has been out since Week 3 and is now nearing a return, getting in limited work with a fibula injury on Wednesday. WR Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) was a DNP on Wednesday. Neither Njoku nor Thompson need to be on fantasy rosters just yet.

Headline: Seahawks signed QB Adrian Martinez to the practice squad.
News Snippet: Martinez has bounced around the 49ers and Jets in the NFL, while winning MVP in the UFL in 2024. He worked out for the Ravens earlier this week but now joins the Seahawks as depth with Sam Darnold (quad) banged up and set to miss Week 9 against the Cardinals.

Headline: Christian Kirk (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Kirk comes out of the 49ers’ bye as a limited practice participant due to a knee issue. He was not targeted in Week 7 after returning off a calf injury and should remain off fantasy rosters even if he plays in Week 9 against the Raiders.

Headline: Reed Blankenship (consussion/hand) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Blankenship has been dealing with a concussion since Week 6 and still has it listed as an injury designation nearly three weeks later. He is also listed with a hand injury. Blankenship will need to progress through concussion protocol to have a chance at playing in Week 9; he is on the wrong side of questionable for now.

Headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said RB Kenneth Gainwell’s usage is getting closer to the “1A, 1B” usage the team envisioned when signing him.
News Snippet: Gainwell saw 25 carries in a run-heavy game against the Falcons in Week 8. Bowles said, “I think we finally got to where we’re utilizing Kenny more and more, and that’s kind of the 1A, 1B we were talking about when we first signed him.” Gainwell saw 50-percent of the snaps for the first time all season last week and now has back-to-back weeks of at least 14 carries. He is still seeing low utilization in the passing game and game script has certainly played a role in his recent role, but it is notable that Bowles mentions the Bucs envisioned a 1A/1B backfield pairing between Bucky Irving and Gainwell. Despite Bowles’ comments, fantasy managers should anticipate Irving operating with the majority of backfield touches, like he did from Weeks 1-6. We will still have to see Gainwell’s usage in a more neutral game script to feel confident about him as a fantasy option moving forward.

Headline: Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Campbell missed the Eagles’ Week 8 game against the Commanders after not practicing all of last week due to hamstring and quad injuries. He starts out this week DNP, along with DBs Michael Carter (abdomen) and Jonathan Jones (hamstring) on the defensive side of the ball. All three will need some kind of practice later in the week to have a chance at reinforcing the Eagles defense in Week 9 against the Giants.

Headline: Jake Elliot (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Elliot was listed as a limited participant for the Eagles’ Wednesday practice. The 31-year-old has made 6-of-7 field goals this season and all 17 extra points. He is still trending to play in Week 9, but if the Eagles add another kicker sometime this week, that would indicate Elliot’s ankle injury is a real issue.

Headline: Trent McDuffie (back) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: McDuffie played through a groin injury in Week 8 and seemingly picked up a new back injury during the game. Rams head coach Sean McVay said McDuffie will be a DNP Wednesday, indicating the 26-year-old’s back issue is more than a minor flare-up. It’s possible he is getting the day off to rest the groin and back injuries, but Rams fans should keep an eye on his practice status the rest of the week. It’s safe to say McDuffie is truly questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.

Headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Rams head coach Sean McVay announced Parkinson would be a DNP on Wednesday. The 27-year-old has been dealing with a rib injury since Week 7, missing the Rams’ Week 8 game against the Chargers. Starting out DNP puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.

Headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Panthers.
News Snippet: Waddle played through a questionable tag with this injury last week, catching 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards and one touchdown against the Chiefs. He apparently made it through the contest without re-injuring himself and can be started as a WR3 this week against the Panthers.

Headline: Pat Bryant (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Panthers.
News Snippet: Bryant’s 21-day practice window has been opened, and it begins with a full session, putting him on track to play in Week 9 against the Panthers. The Broncos’ passing game has severely underperformed expectations. Bryant does not necessarily need to be added in 12-team formats, though he could ultimately compete for No. 2 wide receiver duties.

Headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams must find a way to trade for a wide receiver before the November 10th deadline.
News Snippet: The Rams’ resources are thin. They already traded away their 2027 first- and second-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. They also have just $8,000 in 2026 salary cap space, so restructuring the potential new add’s deal would be required. Atkins believes the Rams should consider Josh Downs as the top option due to his ability to beat man coverage and contribute as a returner. Other options, according to Atkins, include Calvin Ridley, Keenan Allen and Jauan Jennings, “for the likely cost of a Day 3 pick.”

Headline: Raiders released WR Cody White.
News Snippet: Tight end Carter Runyon was activated from injured reserve in a corresponding move. White has eight catches for 112 yards and three scores this year. He also contributes on special teams. The Raiders could ultimately sign him to their practice squad and promote him to the game-day roster this week.

Headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) did not practice on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Dolphins RB3 Kaytron Allen (quad) was limited. At some point, Allen might get a chance to overtake Wright for the No. 2 role, though Wright remains a capable special teams contributor.

Headline: Kadyn Proctor (concussion) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Lions.
News Snippet: The Dolphins’ starting left guard should make his return this week after sitting out in Week 8 against the Patriots. Proctor’s presence will help stabilize the pocket for Malik Willis.

Headline: Christian Watson (rib) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Watson famously left for the hospital in the middle of Week 8’s win over the Panthers, only to return after halftime like a WWE performer. The fact that they’re letting him practice in any capacity today means he should be able to play through the issue in Week 9. We’d expect him to wear a flak jacket for at least a few weeks. Barring a setback in practice, Watson will be a high-variance WR1 for his matchup with the Patriots.

Headline: Malik Willis (groin) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Lions.
News Snippet: Willis did the same during Week 8 practices and ended up running just once against the Patriots. Hopefully, the groin injury continues to improve and his rushing usage returns. Willis remains a QB2 this week against the Lions.

Headline: Bryce Young (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Broncos.
News Snippet: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said after Week 8’s loss to the Packers that Young’s knee injury could be limiting his mobility. The team didn’t list the knee issue on this week’'s injury report, instead adding an ankle injury to the mix. It’s not something that will prevent Young from playing on Sunday, but another lingering ailment could further hamper his mobility. Already in the midst of a two-game slump, Young is back in the middle of the QB2 ranks for Week 9.

Headline: Denzel Boston (calf) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: A limited designation for the first practice of the week is usually nothing to worry about. We’ll assume as much for now. Boston has been racking up targets and air yards without much to show for it in his box scores over the past month. He hasn’t eclipsed 50 yards in a game since Week 4. A date with New Orleans’ struggling defense should help him get back on track as a WR3 for Week 9.

Headline: Caleb Downs (concussion/ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
News Snippet: The Cowboys’ rookie safety and slot defensive back is very banged up. He is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for Week 9 against the Colts at this time.

Headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
News Snippet: The Cowboys’ No. 1 tight end suffered an ankle injury in Week 8 against the Cardinals. Ferguson is not in the TE1 ranks even when he is healthy, but his absence could help others earn a couple of extra targets.

Headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Donaldson aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 7 against the Steelers and did not return. He also entered the league’s concussion protocol after the game. A limited session today means he’s making progress on both fronts. He should be good to go for Week 9. The same is true of Alvin Kamara, who got a rest day today, despite his back injury also being noted on the report. Both backs will mix in behind Kendre Miller on Sunday.

Headline: Mason Taylor (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: It’s likely a maintenance day for Taylor, who tallied three catches on five targets in Week 8. He has been running ahead of rookie Kenyon Sadiq in recent weeks, though his own fantasy has been hit or miss. Taylor has been held under 40 yards in three of his past four appearances. He erupted for 62 yards and two scores in the fourth. Barring a setback in practice, Taylor will be a low-end TE2 for Week 9.

Headline: George Pickens (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
News Snippet: On the plus side, Pickens is no longer listed with a shoulder injury. Hopefully, Pickens upgrades to full participation tomorrow, and puts this hamstring strain behind him. Team owner Jerry Jones told reporters earlier this week that Pickens needs to get the ball more. The squeaky wheel often gets greased. The Cowboys’ Week 9 game against the Colts looks like a solid bounce-back spot.

Headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Jaylen Watson will undergo season-ending shoulder surgery.
News Snippet: This is an unfortunate loss. Watson is the Rams’ No. 2 perimeter cornerback, and No. 1 cornerback Trent McDuffie has been slowed by a groin injury in recent weeks. Watson signed a three-year, $51 million contract with the Rams this offseason. Hopefully, Watson makes a full recovery in time for next season.

Headline: Breece Hall (quad) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Hall is expected to return this week, but a full practice might be required before the team gives him the go-ahead. Hall logged three limited practices last week before being ruled out on Sunday. Barring a setback, we’re still expecting Hall to ramp up to a full session over the next two days. Assuming he does, Hall will likely split work with Braelon Allen, who has been extremely effective as the Jets’ workhorse running back in his absence. Both backs will sit in the RB3 ranks for their Week 9 date with the Chiefs.

Headline: Rams opened Terrance Ferguson’s (ankle) 21-day practice window.
News Snippet: Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters that Ferguson will be limited today. The Rams could get their top receiving tight end back on the field this week, but they have slow-played his rehab thus far. It would be unsurprising to see him sit out this weekend. He should be added where available, though.

Headline: Myles Garrett (knee) will practice on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters that Garrett will be limited today. The team could still give him another couple of weeks to ramp up, but he at least has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Commanders. Garrett underwent surgery on his injured knee back in September.

Headline: Bears placed Kentavius Street on injured reserve with a knee injury.
News Snippet: The Bears’ backup defensive tackle suffered a knee injury in Week 8 against the Seahawks. Whether he has a chance to return this season has not yet been reported. The Bears also signed TE Stephen Carlson to the active roster and DL Earnest Brown to the practice squad.

Headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice
News Snippet: Rice returned from a multi-game absence because of the hamstring injury last week and he’s been on the injury report with the knee issue for most of the year. It doesn’t sound like either injury will prevent him from playing in Week 9. The limited session was likely maintenance. Rice led the Chiefs with eight targets in his first game back on Sunday. He’s been the Chiefs’ only consistently productive pass-catcher when healthy. He will be in the WR1 mix when he takes on the Jets this week.

Headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Kelce looked slightly hobbled by the ankle issue in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos, but he played through it and never missed a meaningful number of snaps. A limited session today means he should be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Jets. Kelce’s numbers are down over the past month, but he’s still seeing enough work to be considered a low-end TE1, especially against a weak Jets defense.

Headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Donaldson aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 7 against the Steelers and did not return. He also entered the league’s conccussion protocl after the game. A limited session today means he’s making progress on both fronts. He should be good to go for Week 9. The same is true of Alvin Kamara, who got a rest day today, despite his back injury also being noted on the report. Both backs will mix in behind Kender Miller on Sunday.

Headline: Saints opened Kelvin Banks’ (ankle) 21-day practice window.
News Snippet: This is a big deal. The Saints’ left tackle earned PFWA All-Rookie Team honors last year. He suffered what was reportedly a “severe” high-ankle sprain earlier this season and underwent surgery to correct the issue. He was initially expected to return sometime in December, but apparently his rehab went very well. Banks is not guaranteed to suit up in Week 9 against the Browns, but he should retake the field soon enough. Banks’ impending return will boost both the Saints’ pass game and run game. Banks was officially limited at Wednesday’s practice.

Headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said James Conner (ankle) will not return from injured reserve this week.
News Snippet: LaFleur could only say the team was taking things “week to week” when asked if Conner will play this year. It sounds like the veteran running back may ultimately miss the entire season. With Jeremiyah Love on IR, Tyler Allgeier will handle the bulk of the backfield touches versus Seattle.

Headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said Cam Skattebo (hamstring) remains day-to-day.
News Snippet: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports that Skattebo once again worked with trainers off to the side at today’s practice. He will be listed as a non-participant. With Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) on injured reserve, Devin Singletary is tentatively in line to start in Week 9 against the Eagles. He would likely be an RB3/FLEX if Skattebo cannot play.

Headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: St. Brown briefly left the Lions’ Week 8 win over the Vikings but managed to finish the game. A limited session today means the rib injury should be a non-issue by Sunday. The Lions should have no issues picking apart Miami’s atrocious defense this week. Per usual. St. Brown will be a high-end WR1.

Headline: Cardinals designated Isaiah Adams (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
News Snippet: The Cardinals’ offensive line has been slowed by injuries this season. Adams’ return is good news. It is unclear whether he will be able to play this week, but he will be back within 21 days at the very least.

Headline: 49ers opened Demarcus Robinson’s (ankle) 21-day practice window.
News Snippet: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Robinson will be limited at today’s practice. This gives him a chance to play in Week 9 against the Raiders. Wide receiver-needy fantasy managers can consider adding him, though his place in the target pecking order is uncertain with Mike Evans (Achilles) recovering.

Headline: Nick Bosa (calf) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Bosa could end up being listed with a knee issue after battling tendinitis earlier this year, but we do not yet have the official injury report. Bosa’s post-bye return to practice tentatively puts him on track to face the Raiders in Week 9.

Headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will not practice on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Samuel remains sidelined by his Week 5 hamstring strain. He still has a chance to resume practicing in time to face the Raiders this weekend, but it would have been nice to see him take the field today. The 49ers were on bye in Week 8.

Headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will not practice on Wednesday.
News Snippet: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said more than a week ago that McCaffrey has a “mild” hamstring strain. Hamstring strains can be finicky. If Kaelon Black is available, add him immediately. McCaffrey still has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Raiders’ soft run defense, but he is ever so slightly in the questionable column at this time.

Headline: David Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 9 against the Chargers.
News Snippet: Per head coach DeMeco Ryans, Montgomery remains week-to-week. He did not practice today and we assume he won’t get on the field in any capacity this week. Woody Marks will make another start. Facing a down-horrific Chargers squad, Marks should finally get going after two underwhelming starts in Montgomery’s absence. He is a locked-in RB2 for Week 9.

Headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not practice on Wednesday.
News Snippet: We had hoped to see Evans practice today, following the 49ers’ Week 8 bye, but evidently, he needs more time to rest and recover. The 49ers’ No. 1 wide receiver should currently be viewed as questionable to play in Week 9 against the Raiders. The 49ers have playoff aspirations, so the team could choose to hold him out this week.

Headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Ravens.
News Snippet: The Jaguars keep many of their injured players limited all week, Meyers included. The move was likely just a conservative measure, given the short practice week. The Jaguars will likely take a run-heavy approach against a Ravens team playing with their QB3. Meyers is just a FLEX, given the expected game script.

Headline: Travon Walker (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Ravens.
News Snippet: Walker was added to the Jaguars’ injury report on Tuesday, apparently having suffered a ribs injury in practice. The Jaguars’ No. 2 edge rusher might not be needed to win an expectedly lopsided affair, but having him on the field will certainly be helpful for the Jaguars D/ST.

Headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Barkley played through the pair of injuries last week, turning 13 carries into 30 yards in a score. While this could just be maintenance for a banged-up veteran, the Eagles are waving the white flag on 2026 by starting Joe Milton at quarterback. If they’re worried about making Barkley’s injuries worse, the team may simply shut him down for the year at some point. Elijah Mitchell is the next man up for Philly if Barkley doesn’t play in Week 9.

Headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Ravens.
News Snippet: Rodriguez remained limited all week, as did many Jaguars on the Week 9 injury report. It seems likely that the team simply took a conservative approach to their Thursday Night Football preparation. Rodriguez could end up being the Jaguars’ starter this week, with Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) labeled a game-time decision after failing to practice all week. Rodriguez warrants RB2 treatment if this is the case. Add him everywhere.

Headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Wicks hasn’t played or practiced since Week 6. It doesn’t look like he has much of a shot at suiting up this week. With a Week 10 bye up next, fantasy managers in even the deepest of leagues can cut Wicks loose.

Headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Smith has been out since Week 6, which was his first game back from a two-week absence. In the middle of a lost season, there’s no reason for the Eagles to rush their star receiver back. We don’t expect him to play this week and it’s possible he’s out for a while longer. Makai Lemon will likely operate as the team’s WR1 once again.

Headline: Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Ravens.
News Snippet: Jaguars coach Liam Coen told reporters earlier today that Tuten will be a game-time decision for this week’s Thursday Night Football game. He also told reporters that Tuten would get in a limited session today. Unfortunately, that did not happen. Tuten logged his third DNP of the week instead. Conversely, Chris Rodriguez (hand) logged three limited sessions and was removed from the injury report. As things currently stand, Tuten is on the wrong side of questionable, while Rodriguez appears to be the likely starter. Rodriguez should be added in all 10- and 12-team leagues.

Headline: Ravens S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
News Snippet: Cornerback Nate Wiggins is questionable with an illness. He did not practice today. Hawkins missed Week 8 with the knee issue and wasn’t able to practice once this week. The Ravens play on Thursday this week and then get an extended break until Monday of Week 10, when they’ll take on the Chargers. The extra time off might help Hawkins get back on the field.

Headline: Justice Hill (groin) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jaguars.
News Snippet: Hill saw eight targets in a blowout loss last week. Third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano peppered him with check-downs, though Hill only managed four catches. With Fagnano making his first career start tomorrow, Hill should continue to rack up targets in Week 9. He’s in the RB4 mix in PPR leagues.

Headline: Mark Andrews (hand) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jaguars.
News Snippet: Andrews has been playing through the hand injury for a few weeks without any issues. He logged three full practices this week. With Joe Fagnano making his first career start for the Ravens tomorrow, we wouldn’t advise playing any Ravens outside of Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers this week.

Headline: Adam Randall (neck) is questionable for Week 9 against the Jaguars.
News Snippet: Randall is currently on injured reserve, so the Ravens will have to activate him tomorrow afternoon if they plan on him playing. He will compete with Rasheen Ali for the RB3 role if he’s ready to return to the field this week. There isn’t any fantasy value to be had here.

Headline: A to Z Sports’ Charles Goldman reports that if the Chiefs trade for a wide receiver, the team “would like to acquire a long-term fixture rather than a one-year rental.”
News Snippet: Chiefs coach Andy Reid told reporters today that general manager Brett Veach has been constantly sharing potential trade targets with the coaching staff for about a month. According to Goldman, the Chiefs could also target additions along the offensive and defensive lines, but he believes the team would “likely have to acquire a receiver through other means” before focusing on the trenches. There aren’t many free agency options right now, though, so it is unclear how this scenario would play out. Goldman notes that Josh Downs and Brian Thomas Jr. “have surfaced in trade discussions.” He does not think the Chiefs will make a move before Sunday, though a move early next week, before the November 10th trade deadline, is still possible.

Headline: Hunter Henry (foot) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Henry could ultimately get in a limited session later in the day, but this certainly looks like a DNP. The veteran tight end injured his foot early in the Pats’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins and did not return. Rookie Eli Raridon will take his spot in the lineup if Henry is unable to play this week. Raridon is averaging an impressive 13.3 yards per catch while mixing in behind Henry this year. He would immediately be in the TE2 mix if Henry is ruled out.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Ravens are acquiring Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals in a deal that is expected to be completed this weekend.
News Snippet: Schefter adds that this trade will not be completed in time for Brissett to play in Week 9’s Thursday Night Football game for the Ravens, but he will make his debut in Week 10 against the Chargers. Brissett’s impending arrival in Baltimore immediately stabilizes the pass-catching corps’ fantasy value. The trade compensation has not yet been revealed, but we expect to know more soon.

Headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Robinson has missed the past two weeks with the hamstring issue. A limited session today puts him on track to return to the lineup against the Bengals on Sunday. Robinson had at least seven carries in every game before going down in Week 6. He will be in the RB4 mix if he gets the green light for Week 9.

Headline: Saints designated Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) to return from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Tyson aggravated his nagging hamstring late in the offseason and was placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 1. He will practice for the first time today. NewOrleans.Football’s Nick Underhill said it’s possible Tyson plays this week, though he immediately mentioned a potential snap count for the rookie. The Saints likely want to ramp Tyson up slowly to avoid another setback. He was limited in Wednesday’s session. Tyson should be stashed in every fantasy format, but managers can’t count on him as even a FLEX play for at least one more week.

Headline: David Montgomery (groin) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Montgomery could still need more time to recover from his Week 5 groin injury. Woody Marks should be expected to start against the Chargers this weekend, at this time. Montgomery technically still has a chance to resume practicing this week, but today likely would have served as the first ramp-up session if he had a good chance of playing.

Headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that Tanner McKee will not start in Week 9 against the Giants.
News Snippet: Joe Milton will start for the Eagles against the Giants this week. McKee’s time under center lasted three games. Unfortunately, he never once threw for more than 215 yards or threw multiple touchdowns. McKee can be dropped in two-quarterback leagues. Milton is a volatile QB2.

Headline: Drew Lock will start for the Seahawks in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
News Snippet: Sam Darnold is considered week-to-week with a quad injury. Lock himself is only barely healthy, having been relegated to emergency QB3 duties because of an eblow issue for the past two games. He’s clearly close enough to full strength if Mike Macdonald is willing to name him the starter on Wednesday. He did note that Jalen Milroe will also get some reps in practice this week. Lock threw for 422 yards and four touchdowns in a little under two full games earlier in the year. Facing a weak Arizona defense, Lock is in the QB2 mix for Week 9.

Headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that Joe Milton will be the Eagles’ starting quarterback in Week 9 against the Giants.
News Snippet: Milton, 26, has spent time with three different teams since the Patriots drafted him in the 2024 NFL Draft’s sixth round. He is a towering, mobile, cannon-armed quarterback with enticing traits. His erratic play can also be frustrating. Milton can be added in two-quarterback leagues, though his range of potential outcomes in his first start is extremely wide. He replaces Tanner McKee after a three-game starting stint.

Headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold (quad) will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
News Snippet: Per Macdonald, Darnold also suffered a rib injury early in the team’s Week 8 loss to the Bears, though that doesn’t appear to be the reason he’s out this week. Darnold is considered week-to-week. Per Macdonald, he won’t go on injured reserve. It’s possible this quad issue is related to the glute issue that sidelined Darnold earlier in the season. Either way, Darnold’s health concerns are now becoming an issue for a Seahawks team that was already struggling to live up to the hype. Drew Lock will draw the start versus Arizona this week. He’ll likely start in Week 10 as well. With two successful appearances under his belt this year, Lock is a somewhat safe QB2 bet for Superflex managers.

Headline: Packers designated Chris Brooks (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Brooks is back at practice and could be officially activated from IR ahead of the Packers’ Week 9 matchup with the Patriots. He would likely take Pierre Strong’s spot in the lineup as Green Bay’s RB3.

Headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Egbuka missed Week 7 with a concussion and a foot injury. He cleared the league’s concussion protocol last week, but the foot issue kept him on ice. A DNP today suggests he will miss another week. However, head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Egbuka worked off to the side today. The team will see how he feels tomorrow. That leaves the door open for him to play, but fantasy managers should at least have backup options in place. If he does suit up, Egbuka would be a high-risk WR3 versus Chicago.

Headline: Liam Coen said Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) will be a game-time decision for Week 9 against the Ravens.
News Snippet: Tuten did not practice on Tuesday. Coen told reporters he would get in a limited session today. Tuten himself told Coen he feels better today and he toughed it out through the injury on Sunday. He appears to be on the right side of questionable for Thursday’s contest, but fantasy managers will want to check inactives before kickoff to be sure. If he can’t go, Chris Rodriguez will get the bulk of the carries for the Jags.

Headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: It’s rare for a player to miss even one game with an illness. It’s even more unheard of for them to miss the next practice. It’s possible Henderson is dealing with something more severe than the flu or a stomach bug. If he isn’t able to play in Week 9, Rhamondre Stevenson will handle the bulk of the backfield touches once again. He touched the ball 22 times on Sunday and would be in line for a similar workload against the Packers.

Headline: A.J. Brown (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Brown’s recurring knee issue flared up during practice last week. He was downgraded to a DNP on Thursday and Friday. The Pats then ruled him out over the weekend. Brown has been dealing with this injury for years, and it was something the Pats acknowledged when they traded for him in the offseason. It wouldn’t be surprising for the team to give him multiple weeks off in preparation for a playoff run. Head coach Mike Vrabel sidestepped a question about putting Brown back on injured reserve. At a minimum, we’re not expecting Brown to suit up this week.

Headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Micah Parsons (knee) is a “full go” to do individual work at practice.
News Snippet: That doesn’t mean Parsons is a “full go” for Week 9 against the Patriots, however, as the pass rusher comes back from a season-ending knee injury in 2025. Parsons could return soon for a Green Bay defense that ranks 12th in pressure rate and 16th in quick pressure rate on the season. Look for the team to ease Parsons into action to make sure he’s OK for the final stretch of the regular season.

Headline: Jack Campbell said he has full movement in his lower body.
News Snippet: Campbell, who was carted off with a frightening neck injury in Week 8 against the Vikings, said in a statement that he is recovering. “I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time,” Campbell’s statement reads, in part. “I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.” Campbell is likely out for the rest of the season, a blow to a Detroit defense that has struggled against both the pass and the run this season.

Headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) is “trending in the right direction.”
News Snippet: Hall, barring setbacks in practice, should be OK for Week 9 against the Chiefs. What his workload will look like is another question entirely. Braelon Allen has established himself as an efficient, tough runner over the past few weeks, and could remain the Jets’ lead rusher while Hall takes on most pass-catching opportunities. Though Hall should have some kind of floor in Week 9, he probably doesn’t have much of a ceiling unless the Jets decided to phase out Allen.

Headline: Jets placed Garrett Wilson in the NFL’s concussion protocol.
News Snippet: He was officially a DNP for Wednesday’s practice. Wilson sustained a head injury in Week 8 against the Raiders and now appears to be a long shot for Week 9. Wilson this season has accounted for 27 percent of the Jets’ targets and 38 percent of the team’s air yards. His absence would make both Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper flex-viable for Week 9, along with Mason Taylor. Cooper is coming off a game in which he saw no targets while running a route on 75 percent of the Jets’ drop backs.

Headline: Jets placed Garrett Wilson in the NFL’s concussion protocol.
News Snippet: Wilson sustained a head injury in Week 8 against the Raiders and now appears to be a long shot for Week 9. Wilson this season has accounted for 27 percent of the Jets’ targets and 38 percent of the team’s air yards. His absence would make both Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper flex-viable for Week 9, along with Mason Taylor. Cooper is coming off a game in which he saw no targets while running a route on 75 percent of the Jets’ drop backs.

Headline: Cleveland.com’s Mary Kay Cabot said the “vibe” is that Shedeur Sanders will start in Week 9 against the Saints.
News Snippet: Cabot said it would be a challenge for Deshaun Watson to clear the NFL’s concussion protocol by Saturday and suit up for Sunday’s game. Watson suffered a head injury in Week 8 against the Steelers and reported concussion symptoms on Tuesday, according to the Browns. Sanders in 2025 was the most inaccurate quarterback in the league and struggled to support fantasy-relevant pass catchers. Harold Fannin could see a boost with Sanders under center after Sanders targeted the tight end relentlessly during his 2025 starts.

Headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Jonathan Taylor remains on the Colts roster.
News Snippet: Steichen mostly dodged questions about why the Colts would play Taylor in Week 9 if the team was in talks with contenders who might want to acquire the star running back before the NFL’s trade deadline. “Teams call all the time,” Steichen told reports. He said the team was focused on the Cowboys, their opponents in Week 9. Taylor seems more than likely to be dealt to another team in the coming weeks. That could be the Vikings, Bengals, Seahawks, or another contending team in need of backfield help.

Headline: Tyler Huntley (toe) is out for the remainder of the season.
News Snippet: Further evaluation of Huntley’s toe injury showed it was a season ender. That leaves the Ravens desperate at quarterback for the remainder of the season. Against the Jaguars on Thursday night the team is likely to start Joe Fagnano. It’s unclear who will serve as the team’s backup quarterback this week or going forward. Zay Flowers goes from an elite weekly fantasy option to something closer to a WR3 in this degraded offensive environment. Derrick Henry’s prospects take a major knock too.

Headline: Browns placed Deshaun Watson in the NFL’ s concussion protocol.
News Snippet: Watson took a hit to the head in the first half of the Browns’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers. He was evaluated for a brain injury and re-entered the game. He then reported concussion-like symptoms on Tuesday and entered the protocol on Wednesday. It would be somewhat surprising if Watson is able to clear the protocol in time for the Browns’ Week 9 matchup against the Saints. That would likely mean Shedeur Sanders would get the starting nod against New Orleans. Sanders should only be rostered in superflex formats for now.

Headline: Brandon Aiyuk submitted paperwork to the NFL for his reinstatement.
News Snippet: Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, confirmed the development on Wednesday, and said Aiyuk would report to the 49ers on Friday. That could expedite his release from the team so he could seek employment with another, presumably wideout-needy NFL team. Aiyuk’s erratic behavior over the past year and questions about his conditioning could prevent some teams from pursuing him. “Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field,” Rosenhaus said. He had been closely linked to the Commanders before a series of online meltdowns in the offseason. The Rams could be in the market for Aiyuk with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined indefinitely. Aiyuk is still unlikely to have any fantasy value this season.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Mack Hollins (calf) will return to practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Hollins has been on injured reserve for a month with a calf injury. With a full practice today he’ll have a good chance of suiting up in Week 9 against the Packers. Hollins will likely function as Drake Maye’s primary downfield option if A.J. Brown remains sidelined. Hollins’ return dings the fantasy prospects of DeMario Douglas, who has an 18 percent target share and a 19 percent air yards share over the team’s past three games. Hollins will be flex viable in deeper formats.

Headline: Eagles waived CB Jakorian Bennett.
News Snippet: Bennett was acquired by the Eagles in a swap with the Raiders before the start of last season. The 26-year-old played 98 defensive snaps in two seasons for Philly, spending all of the 2026 season on injured reserve with a knee injury. The Eagles now waive Bennett from injured reserve.

Headline: The Denver Gazette’s Chris Tomasson said “indications point to Broncos WR Pat Bryant returning to practice this week.”
News Snippet: Bryant has missed the Broncos’ last four games after being placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury. The 23-year-old receiver is eligible to return whenever the Broncos deem him ready to do so, and his practicing this week would mean the team has opened his 21-day return window. Bryant has caught nine passes for 133 yards and one touchdown and was third among Broncos receivers in routes run (91) through the first four weeks of the season. He could make for an interesting stash in deeper leagues, but fantasy managers shouldn’t rush to put him in their lineups whenever he does return.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Brian Thomas Jr. “has been the area of interest for a lot of other teams.”
News Snippet: Thomas is once again the subject of trade talks as next week’s trade deadline rapidly approaches. The 24-year-old receiver, who broke out for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie, has earned just 22 targets through seven games this season and has a 10-117-2 line. With so many wide receiver-needy teams out there, it’s hard to imagine the Jaguars holding Thomas, who has become more of an afterthought in the offense, but they’ve resisted trading him over the last year despite multiple teams showing interest.

Headline: Saints released K Daniel Carlson.
News Snippet: Carlson has converted 8-of-12 field goals this season and is 16-for-18 on PATs. The veteran kicker who is known for his big leg has seen all four of his misses come on distances of 50-plus yards, but that was more than enough for the Saints to look in a different direction. Practice squad kicker Charlie Smyth, who converted 12 of his 16 field goal attempts for the Saints last season has a chance to be the next man up when the Saints take on the Browns in Week 9.

Headline: Ravens placed K Tyler Loop (groin) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Loop will be sidelined for at least the next four weeks after suffering a right groin injury in Sunday’s loss to the Bills. The second-year kicker competed for the starting kicker job in camp and has struggled during parts of this season. He has converted on 13 of his 17 field goal attempts this year, with his four misses all coming from inside 50 yards. Veteran Jake Moody is set to take over in Loop’s absence when the Ravens face the Jaguars on Thursday night. Loop will be eligible to return in Week 14 when the Ravens play host to the Buccaneers.

Headline: Giants signed CB Greg Newsome to a three-year, $46 million contract extension.
News Snippet: Newsome signed a one-year $8 million contract with the Giants this offseason and is now being rewarded for his strong play during the first half of this season. The 26-year-old corner has allowed just 174 receiving yards on 26 targets this season, per PFF, earning a coverage grade of 66.1. He has been one of the league’s better outside corners this season and will now be under contract with the Giants through the 2029 season.

Headline: Bills released DB C.J. Gardner-Johnson.
News Snippet: Shortly after being reinstated from suspension for a spitting incident in Week 6 against the Raiders, Gardner-Johnson is now in search of a new home. The 28-year-old safety started all six games he appeared in for the Bills this season, earning a PFF defensive grade of 55.2 while allowing 11 receptions for 132 yards and a touchdown on 15 targets. Gardner-Johnson has played for four different teams since 2024 and is now free to sign with anyone willing to take on the 28-year-old vet.

Headline: Commanders placed DT Javon Kinlaw (knee) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Kinlaw was ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Eagles and will now miss at least the next four games after landing on IR. Kinlaw has tallied 13 tackles and one sack for the Commanders this season and will be eligible to return in Week 13 when the Commanders take on the Titans.

Headline: Commanders placed RB Jeremy McNichols (foot) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: McNichols is believed to have suffered a severe foot injury in Sunday night’s win over the Eagles. While he is still seeking additional opinions, it was reported on Monday that he is expected to miss multiple months, which could mean this is a season-ender. McNichols has spent the last three seasons with the Commanders, contributing primarily on special teams while also mixing in for an occasional offensive play.

Headline: Colts signed DT Adetomiwa Adebawore to a two-year, $35 million contract extension.
News Snippet: Adebawore, 25, is in the midst of a breakout season for the Colts. After setting career highs in tackles (36), TFLs (5), and sacks (4.0) last season, the fourth-year pro has already tallied four sacks and four TFLs in his first eight games of this season. While the Colts are in the middle of a rebuild, the decision to sign Adebawore to an extension means he’s one of the players they hope to build around in the years ahead. He is now under contract through the 2028 season.

Headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Tyler Huntley (toe) could be placed on injured reserve.
News Snippet: The decision on whether or not to place Huntley on injured reserve could come in the next few days as the Ravens prepare to play the Jaguars on Thursday. With Lamar Jackson (thumb) expected to be placed on IR and possibly be out for the rest of the season, Huntley landing on IR would mean the Ravens would be starting their third-string QB (or worse) for at least the next four weeks. Rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano has already been named as the starter for Thursday’s game against the Jaguars, but was seen sporting an ankle brace in Tuesday’s practice. While he’s expected to play through it, the Ravens could be forced to play either Austin Reed or Kedon Slovis, who signed with the team earlier this week.

Headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Joe Fagnano will start in Week 9 against the Jaguars.
News Snippet: The 25-year-old rookie UDFA will make the starting lineup on Thursday night against the Jaguars’ top-flight defense under the lights. Fagnano predictably struggled in the two-and-a-half quarters he played against the Bills last week, throwing for just 91 yards on 10-of-21 passes while also throwing a pick and taking three sacks. While it’s possible a short week of prep as the team’s QB1 could yield marginally better results, this projects to be a tough matchup for Fagnano and the rest of the Ravens’ offensive players. Fagnano will not be on the fantasy radar this week, and Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers will both be docked a few spots in fantasy rankings due to the downgrade at QB.

Headline: Speaking on the Pat McAfee Show, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said “I was told the Dallas Cowboys aren’t trading George Pickens.”
News Snippet: Rapoport added that “as of right now, there’s nothing there,” as far as a potential trade is concerned. Pickens, who is playing out the season on the franchise tag, hasn’t produced at the level he did in 2025 when he broke out for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns, but he remains a focal point in the offense despite his underwhelming production. Pickens still ranks 14th in the league among all receivers in targets and is 12th in total air yards. Despite the Cowboys’ disappointing 3-5 record, they remain in the race to win what has been an underwhelming NFC East. With team owner Jerry Jones saying earlier that Pickens needs to be targeted more, it’s safe to assume he will remain with the Cowboys for the season.

Headline: Cardinals placed Jeremiyah Love (ankle) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: The new injury Love picked up in Week 8’s win over the Cowboys has been diagnosed as a high-ankle sprain and will sideline Love for a minimum of four weeks. Love, who has been dealing with multiple ankle injuries this season, has had a tough start to his NFL career. In six career games he’s rushed for 268 yards and one touchdown on 76 carries, while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and another score. His injury comes as Bam Knight is in the league’s concussion protocol, leaving Tyler Allgeier and Evan Hull as the only two healthy backs on the Cardinals’ 53-man roster. Allgeier could be in line for a significant role in Week 9 against the Seahawks if Knight is unable to clear protocol, and veteran Jerome Ford could also be promoted from the practice squad in the coming days. Love will not be eligible to return until Week 13 against the Eagles.

Headline: Joe Fagnano was seen wearing an ankle guard/brace during Tuesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Head coach Jesse Minter said on Monday that Fagnano was “dealing with some things physically,” but the rookie UDFA is still expected to make his first career start on Thursday against the Jaguars. Fagnano was wearing the guard/brace on his right ankle, but was on the field practicing with the team. The Ravens recently signed Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis to the practice squad, with Reed looking like the most likely backup to Fagnano on Thursday night. Hopefully the Ravens aren’t forced to go to fourth QB in less than a week, but Fagnano clearly isn’t operating at 100 percent.

Headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) was not spotted at Tuesday’s practice.
News Snippet: After being an estimated DNP on Monday, Tuten was not spotted at Tuesday’s practice. With the Jaguars playing Thursday, this is a bit concerning for his Week 9 availability, as he will likely need to get in a limited practice on Wednesday if he hopes to suit up. In the event he can’t go, Chris Rodriguez, who ran for 41 yards and a touchdown on six carries last week, would be in line to handle a significant workload against the Ravens.

Headline: The Athletic’s Ted Nguyen said Kyler Murray has been “constantly late on his reads,” leading to misfires.
News Snippet: Nguyen studied Murray’s film in the Minnesota offense and noted the veteran is often late to recognize an open pass catcher. That could be related to Murray’s clear discomfort in Kevin O’Connell’s offense, as Nguyen noted. “When his first read doesn’t open up, he holds the ball and runs backward,” leading to drive-killing sacks. That’s exactly what unfolded a few times in high-leverage situations against the Lions in Week 8. Justin Jefferson on Sunday appeared frustrated by Kyler’s inability to make the proper reads on critical downs. All of this has an outsized impact on Murray’s fantasy prospects. He now ranks 31st among QBs in expected fantasy points per game, below Bo Nix and Daniel Jones.

Headline: Ravens worked out QB Adrian Martinez, formerly of the Jets.
News Snippet: Martinez, who played four seasons at Nebraska and one at Kansas State in college, was the UFL MVP in 2024. He’s had stints with the Jets and 49ers, appearing in one NFL game. The Ravens are shoring up their QB room after Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) went down in Week 8. The Ravens on Tuesday signed journeyman QB Kedon Slovis.

Headline: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said George Pickens “needs the ball coming in his direction more.”
News Snippet: Jones apparently isn’t happy with Pickens’ usage through Week 8. Pickens has been targeted on 22 percent of his pass routes on the season, well below CeeDee Lamb’s 34 percent rate. He’s accounted for 31 percent of the team’s air yards, nearly the same rate he saw in 2025. In the Cowboys’ humiliating Week 8 loss to the Cardinals, Pickens had nine targets, one short of Lamb’s ten. Perhaps Jerry has not adequately studied the spreadsheets. Either way, Pickens remains an upside WR2 headed into Week 9.

Headline: Ravens signed QB Kedon Slovis from the Packers practice squad.
News Snippet: Slovis could, unbelievably, get the start Thursday night against the Jaguars with Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) out, and Joe Fagnano (ankle) iffy to suit up. If Fagnano can play, Slovis would presumably serve as Baltimore’s backup. Fagnano completed 48 percent of his passes for 91 yards and a pick last week against the Bills. Look for the Ravens to be ultra run-heavy against Jacksonville, one of the league’s best run defenses. It will be tough to trust anyone in the Ravens offense as a viable fantasy option for now.

Headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said the team’s backfield touch distribution will be a “moving target.”
News Snippet: Mike Washington, Jr. in Week 8 against the Jets took over as the team’s lead rusher, logging 25 carries to just two carries for Ashton Jeanty. While Kubiak said after the game that Jeanty would remain a part of the offense, it’s clear the Raiders are willing to experiment with backfield touches. “You see where your team is at and who’s playing the best ball at the time. It’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. They’ve been changing at guard, they change up front defensively, they change at corner,” Kubiak said. “That’s the NFL. We have a young roster and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best. But your 11, whether you’re playing really well or not playing well at all, it’s always going to change a little bit.” The Raiders through Week 8 rank dead last in EPA per rush and second to last in rushing success rate. Jeanty should remain viable as long as he’s the team’s primary pass catcher out of the backfield. Jeanty ranks fifth among all RBs in expected fantasy points per game.

Headline: Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich said he “assumes” Breece Hall will remain the team’s lead back when he returns from injury.
News Snippet: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn has knocked down suggestions that the Jets would trade Hall before the league’s trade deadline, as Braelon Allen continues as one of the NFL’s most productive rushers. When asked about how the backfield might look when Hall returns from his quad injury, Reich seemed to say Hall would remain the de facto lead runner. “Well, that’s obviously coach’s decision, but they’re both the guy … I mean, that’s a good problem to have,” Reich said. “That’s coach’s decision, but to me … Breece is our guy. I’m assuming Breece is our guy, you know what I mean? He’s one of the best in the NFL, but I think what’s been so excited is like, oh my gosh, we’ve got two of them. I mean, we’ve got two. This Braelon guy, he’s a beast as well.” Allen this season ranks third among running backs in rushing success rate; 11th in rush yards over expected per attempt; eighth in yards after contact per rush; and over the past three weeks he ranks eighth among RBs in expected fantasy points per game, proving the haters wrong along the way. Hall is expected to return to action this week against the Chiefs.

Headline: Zach Charbonnet rushed six times for 23 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears, adding six yards on three receptions.
News Snippet: Charbonnet drew the start but saw four fewer opportunities than rookie Jadarian Price, the latter of whom led the team in rush yards and touches. Expect the two to continue operating in a near-even timeshare moving forward, leaving Charbonnet in shaky FLEX territory ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the Cardinals.

Headline: Jadarian Price rushed 10 times for 29 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears, adding eight yards on two receptions.
News Snippet: It was Zach Charbonnet that drew the start for the Seahawks in his first game since tearing his ACL last year, but it was the talented rookie that led the team in opportunities. Price was making his first appearance since going on the injured reserve with a chest injury suffered in Week 2, and while he led the team in yardage and carries, George Holani remained involved in clear passing situations and Charbonnet is liable to see his role continue to grow with each healthy game. Price will be a shaky FLEX option in a better matchup against the Cardinals in Week 9.

Headline: Sam Darnold completed 17-of-34 passes for 188 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Seahawks’ 34-17, Week 8 loss to the Bears, adding 20 yards on two rushes.
News Snippet: Darnold really struggled through consistent pressure from Dennis Allen’s aggressive defensive front as the Seahawks gained just 252 yards of total offense. Things looked manageable in the first half while Darnold leaned heavily on alpha wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, feeding his top option for 92 yards before the break. Allen’s second half adjustments all but removed JSN from the offense, holding him to just 26 yards after the break. Week 8 went down as only the third game of the 2026 season in which Darnold threw multiple touchdowns, leaving him outside QB2 range and on waiver wires ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the Cardinals.

Headline: Kalif Raymond caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Bears’ Week 8 win over the Seahawks, adding 39 yards on one carry.
News Snippet: Raymond’s lone “carry” came on a third-and-long in the fourth quarter in a three-point game, with the play ruled a rush attempt following a slightly backwards toss on a quick swing pass to the perimeter. Raymond did the rest as he turned on the jets for a 39-yard gain to the five, which D’Andre Swift would punch in for the second of his three rushing scores on the evening. Raymond remains unlikely to match his early-season exploits but can be stashed in case of injury to Luther Burden, Rome Odunze, or Colston Loveland.

Headline: Luther Burden caught 7-of-9 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 8 win over the Seahawks.
News Snippet: Burden’s opening drive score was the first touchdown surrendered by the Seahawks on an opening possession in the previous 26 games, finishing tied with tight end Colston Loveland for the team lead in targets while catching the only passing score from quarterback Caleb Williams. He continues to operate as the team’s top option through the air in a role that is most malleable, which can either be concentrated on the short areas against zone or extended in the vertical against man. Burden is a WR2 in a pass-funnel matchup against the Buccaneers in Week 9.

Headline: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-6 targets for 87 yards in the Bears’ Week 8 win over the Seahawks.
News Snippet: Odunze was almost nonexistent in the first half, catching his first pass, an 18-yard reception over the middle of the field, with just under five minutes remaining in the second quarter. The Bears exploited the attention paid to Luther Burden and Colston Loveland after the half, with Odunze catching three passes for chunk gains in the third quarter to help position the team for their sixth victory. Odunze remains unlikely to challenge for the team lead in targets on a weekly basis while playing alongside Burden and Loveland, but his big play ability keeps him in the FLEX discussion, for the time being. That could change in a more favorable matchup through the air in Week 9 against the Buccaneers, where Odunze will be a WR3.

Headline: D’Andre Swift rushed 27 times for 69 yards and three touchdowns in the Bears’ Week 8 win over the Seahawks, adding 10 yards on two receptions.
News Snippet: Swift managers were sweating early as he alternated drives with Roschon Johnson. Those worries were swiftly erased as the veteran lead back played almost the entirety of the second half, scoring all three of his short yardage touchdowns after the break. The three trips to paint marked his second game with three touchdowns through the first eight weeks, now the only player in the league with multiple three-touchdown games. Swift will be a matchup-based RB2 when the Bears host the Buccaneers in Week 9.

Headline: Caleb Williams completed 24-of-34 passes for 247 yards and one touchdown in the Bears’ 34-17, Week 8 win over the Seahawks, adding one yard on two carries.
News Snippet: Williams marched the Bears down the field for a 17-play opening possession touchdown, snapping a 26-game streak in which the Seahawks kept opponents out of the end zone on first possessions in the process. The two teams traded defensive stops for much of the remainder of the first half before the Bears opened the flood gates after the break, vaulting to a 6-2 record and now just half a game behind the Vikings for the lead in the NFC North. Williams’ ball placement was impeccable in this one, the most notable of which came just after the half on three absolute dimes to Rome Odunze for chunk gains. Two surging teams meet in Week 9 when the Bears host the pass-funnel Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football, where Williams will remain a back end QB1.

Headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
News Snippet: The veteran receiver played through both ailments in Week 8 but was limited to only 54 percent of the team’s offensive snaps in a blowout win. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status in the coming days, with the expectation that he continues to play through the injuries against the Ravens on Thursday Night Football.

Headline: Ravens worked out QB Adrian Martinez, formerly of the Jets.
News Snippet: Martinez, who played four seasons at Nebraska and one at Kansas State in college, was the the UFL MVP in 2024. He’s had stints with the Jets and 49ers, appearing in one NFL game. The Ravens are shoring up their QB room after Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) went down in Week 8. The Ravens on Tuesday signed journeyman QB Kedon Slovis.

Headline: AJ Barner caught 2-of-5 targets for 23 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: Barner is far from fantasy consideration having only one game through eight appearances with more than a modest five targets while failing to notch a single receiving touchdown. Fantasy managers can safely return him to the waiver wire in all formats.

Headline: Tory Horton caught 3-of-6 targets for 26 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: Horton took more massive hits than he had receptions in this one, with Sam Darnold placing him in harm’s way on more than one occasion. He was already fighting through nagging injuries entering the contest but gave it a go with Rashid Shaheed ruled out, with this game likely doing nothing to help him in that regard. Despite finishing second on the team in receiving behind alpha Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Horton is not a startable fantasy asset ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the division rival Cardinals.

Headline: Cooper Kupp caught 1-of-3 targets for seven yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: Kupp was unable to take advantage of the absence of fellow receiver Rashid Shaheed but did cash in for his second touchdown of the season. Kupp’s days of consistent fantasy production are long behind him as the Seahawks head into a Week 9 divisional meeting against the Cardinals approaching must-win territory.

Headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 6-of-11 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: Smith-Njigba was the entire offense in the first half, accumulating 92 yards through the air while the rest of the offense managed only two, including his receiving touchdown. Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen made adjustments after the break that confined JSN to only 26 additional yards the rest of the way. Smith-Njigba now has seven 100-yard receiving games in eight appearances as he extended his league-leading yardage totals, far and away the top overall wide receiver in fantasy circles. That position will not change ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the Cardinals.
